title: The Indian mathematician who found the tallest mountain on Earth
hook: An Indian mathematician measured the tallest mountain on Earth, but the name went to a man who never saw it.
summary: Radhanath Sikdar's calculations showed Peak XV was the world's highest, yet it was named for George Everest, who never saw it and objected to the name.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Radhanath Sikdar, Indian mathematician with the Great Trigonometrical Survey, credited with identifying Peak XV as the highest; height announced 1856 as 29,002 ft.
Britannica / Royal Geographical Society: Mount Everest named in 1865 after Sir George Everest, who objected to the name and never saw the mountain.

lines.text: An Indian mathematician measured the tallest mountain on Earth.
In eighteen fifty-two, Radhanath Sikdar worked for the British survey of India.
Surveyors measured angles from far away, and he did the maths.
lines.caps: Surveyors *measured | angles from *far away, | he did the *maths

lines.text: His numbers showed Peak Fifteen was higher than any known mountain.
lines.caps: His *numbers | showed Peak *Fifteen | was *higher | than any *other

lines.text: Its height was announced in eighteen fifty-six: twenty-nine thousand feet.
Then it was named after George Everest, who never saw it.
He had even objected to the name.
The finder got no name. The mountain got a stranger's.

post.caption:
Radhanath Sikdar's maths put Peak XV above every mountain known, yet the name went to someone else.
Should Everest be called something else?
